title: Structs, references and value semantics
summary: Value types, pass by value vs reference vs const reference, and member functions.
hints: Take the point by reference: `Point& p`. Then `p.x += dx;` changes the caller's point. Without the `&` you would modify a private copy.
`const Point&` parameters are read-only views of the caller's objects, with no copy. Build the result with `return {x, y};`. For `manhattan`, `std::abs` from `<cstdlib>` handles the absolute values.

For `contains`, check `p.x >= r.top_left.x && p.x < r.top_left.x + r.width`, and the same for y. In `Counter`, member functions can read and write `total_` directly; `value()` is marked `const` because it does not modify the object.
